clue.text: Frightful prude in villa near Bootle?

indicators.note: frightful suggests something mangled or made a mess of, so these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful prig living in a villa just outside Bootle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightful' is the anagram signal. Bootle is a town on Merseyside bordering Liverpool, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Liverpool lives in the city that borders Bootle, hence a native of the neighbourhood.

clue.text: One loafing around university is less likely to succeed

indicators.note: around tells us one piece surrounds the other, here the comparative wrapping the letter for university

parts.note: a runner at longer odds is less likely to win

explanation.surface: A layabout at college is judged a poor bet for success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts U inside LONGER, as in longer odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is an idler who lazes about, so a loafing person.

clue.text: Lively musical student out east

indicators.note: out says something is dropped, here the compass letter for east is removed

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber stage musical
L is a learner, the plate shown by a student driver

explanation.surface: An energetic drama student leaves for the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops E from EVITAL (EVITA plus L), leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital can mean full of energy and life, a synonym for spirited.

clue.text: Uncluttered state of cabin, say, in English vessel

parts.note: a cabin is an example of a room, hence 'say'
taken as written
SS, steamship, prefixes a vessel's name

explanation.surface: Describing how tidy a cabin is aboard a British ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaciousness is the quality of having plenty of space, an uncluttered condition.

clue.text: Chaldean birthplace of the French language?

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees was Abraham's birthplace in Genesis
du is French for 'of the'

explanation.surface: Asking which tongue began in ancient Chaldea and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national tongue of Pakistan, a South Asian speech.

clue.text: Post pound, not penny, for meal

indicators.note: pound, not penny says the letter for one coin replaces the letter for the other

parts.note: a puncheon is a short upright timber post
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: An instruction about mailing money to pay for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' swaps the P of PUNCHEON for L. 'Post' looks like mailing but is a timber post.
explanation.definitionFit: Luncheon is a formal word for the midday repast.

clue.text: Help to clothe many beginning to get cold

indicators.note: to clothe means to wrap around, so one piece goes outside the others

parts.note: aid means help
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, crosswordese for many

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Advice to wrap up lots of people as they start to feel chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to clothe' puts L and G inside AID.
explanation.definitionFit: Algid is a rare medical word meaning chilly or icy.

clue.text: Working relation's reprehensible behaviour

parts.note: a machine that is going is working
a son is a relation; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A family member at work behaves badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are improper or suspicious activities, misconduct of a dubious kind.

clue.text: The compiler may be English or Irish

definitions.meaning: the person who devises a crossword
English and Irish are breeds of gundog of that name

explanation.definitionFit: A crossword compiler and a breed of gundog share this one name.

clue.text: "Like the bloodless snow on Linden"? No marks

definitions.text: Like the bloodless snow on Linden
definitions.meaning: from Thomas Campbell's poem Hohenlinden, where the snow on Linden lay bloodless and unmarked by feet
nobody has walked over it, leaving no footprints

explanation.definitionFit: Campbell's poem calls the snow unstepped-on, and ground no feet have crossed bears no prints.

clue.text: Musical lexicographer in leafy road

definitions.meaning: Sir George ... compiled the famous Dictionary of Music and Musicians
a street name for a road lined with trees

explanation.definitionFit: Grove edited the music dictionary, and a grove is a small wood, often used as a street name.

clue.text: Half of bitter — that's for the angler's guide

parts.note: in northern England a gill is a half pint, as of bitter beer
i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A half pint of beer is what a fishing guide gets paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British beer; in parts of northern England a gill means half a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a Scottish attendant who helps people fishing or shooting.

clue.text: "The Mysterious Death of the Carrier in W.I."?

definitions.text: "The Mysterious Death of the Carrier in W.I."?

parts.words: "The Mysterious Death of the Carrier in W.I."?
parts.note: a title that reads like a detective novel, about an unexplained killing in the Women's Institute

explanation.surface: The title of a cosy murder mystery set among village ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: W.I. is the Women's Institute, a British women's community organisation; the title is the kind given to a puzzle-the-killer novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective story where the reader tries to identify the murderer.

clue.text: Compete again with wife in critical examination

parts.note: to vie is to compete, so re-vie is to compete again

explanation.surface: A couple enter a contest again and are scrutinised.
explanation.definitionFit: A review is an assessment or appraisal, a careful look at something.

clue.text: Vehicle security for the forward-looking

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a guard provides security

explanation.surface: A security van serves progressive clients.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard are those leading new developments, the avant-garde.

clue.text: Bliss, possibly, for fellow model riding mare

indicators.note: riding says one piece sits on top of another, the model on the horse

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow or joint, as in co-worker
m is the abbreviation for mare in horse-racing form
a poser is someone who poses, like a model

explanation.surface: Delight at seeing a colleague who models sitting astride a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer and Master of the Queen's Music; 'Bliss' pretends to be happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss wrote music, an example of a musical creator.

clue.text: Devout woman upset about curate's first symbolic representation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier pieces go round the letter from the curate

parts.note: pi is short for pious, devout

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Margot is a woman's name

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word curate's

explanation.surface: A pious lady is distressed over a clergyman's debut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads the woman's name upwards in this down entry; 'about' wraps the pious pair and that reversed name round the curate's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A pictogram is a picture standing for a word or idea, as in early writing systems.

clue.text: President supports member, being theoretical rather than practical

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece supports another by sitting beneath it

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
the chair presides over a meeting

explanation.surface: The head of a club backs one of its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts CHAIR below ARM in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic theorises from comfort without real experience.

clue.text: Chaplain's office in a government building

definitions.meaning: the work of a clergyman, his pastoral calling
a department of state, or the building housing it

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a pastor's service and a department of state.

clue.text: Cleaned a bike without parking

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the bike surrounds the parking letter

parts.note: a moped is a small motorbike
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Someone washed a motorbike while away from the car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: MOPED goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop is to wipe a floor clean, so mopped is wiped up.

clue.text: Witness at police station sounding dramatic

indicators.note: sounding tells us to say the phrase out loud and hear another word

parts.note: see (witness) plus nick, British slang for a police station

explanation.surface: Someone watching at the station sounds theatrical.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for a police station; SEE NICK said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic can mean theatrical, relating to stage scenery or striking effect.

clue.text: A symbol of mourning when gas covers the battlefield

indicators.note: covers means one piece wraps around another, the gas round the town

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas
Ypres in Belgium was a major battlefield of the First World War

explanation.surface: Grief's emblem as gas drifts over a war zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress tree is traditionally planted in graveyards as an emblem of grief.

clue.text: Application from union leader held by constables covering East End

indicators.note: covering means the force surrounds a further letter as well
held by means the union's leader sits inside the force

parts.note: police constables, collectively the police

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of union
End picks the final letter of East

explanation.surface: A trade unionist detained by officers patrolling London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts U into POLICE; 'covering' also puts T, the end of East, inside. The East End is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A poultice is a soft moist dressing applied to the body to soothe inflammation.

clue.text: Lighter carried by an admirer

definitions.meaning: something that gives light, a hand lamp
someone with unrequited love is said to carry a flame for the person

explanation.definitionFit: A portable lamp and the flame held for a beloved in the idiom carry a torch.

clue.text: Lump requiring young woman to have surgery

parts.note: doll is slang for an attractive young woman
an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A lump that means a girl must have an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless blob of something soft, like food.

clue.text: Strange jargon from the Devil in Goethe's Faust

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are drawn out of the following words

explanation.surface: Odd talk taken from Mephistopheles in Goethe's Faust.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a foreign or unfamiliar speech or vocabulary.

clue.text: Smart politician here in ancient Rome

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, a politician of that party
hic is Latin for here

explanation.surface: A well-dressed senator in classical Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant.

clue.text: Wrongdoing is a mistake!

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a sinful deed and a simple slip.

clue.text: Giving support to woman in Yemeni city church

indicators.note: in shows the woman goes inside the city

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen
her refers to a woman
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Backing a woman in a church in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherence is steady attachment or loyalty to a cause, the act of backing it.

clue.text: Not enough food for diminutive people

definitions.meaning: a meagre ration, an insufficient allowance

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means scanty rations, and literally small members of the public.
